recipes.name: Seared Scallops with Jalapeño Vinaigrette
ingredients_raw: 1 large jalapeno pepper, seeded and membranes removed
salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
2 oranges, peeled and cut in between sections as segments

steps.text: Place jalapeño, rice vinegar, olive oil, and mustard into a blender. Purée on high until mixture is completely liquefied, 1 to 2 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.

Season scallops with sea salt and cayenne pepper. Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over high heat. Place scallops into the skillet and cook until browned, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate. Garnish scallops with orange segments and drizzle jalapeño vinaigrette over top.

raw_recipe.headline: Seared Scallops with Jalapeño Vinaigrette
raw_recipe.description: Chef John's seared scallops and oranges are coated with a versatile jalapeño vinaigrette that's so good, you may want to make it as a stand-alone salad dressing!

review.reviewBody: This is a keeper! One of the best recipes I have made in a long, long time. Perfect as is - no changes are needed at all. Make sure your scallops are really dry - season them well and into a screaming hot pan. Don't move them until you flip them. You want to get them good and crispy on the outside. So delicious! Try them - you won't regret making this recipe! Enjoy!

Delicious!! Have made it two times. Second time added a second jalapeño and more cayenne pepper. The spicy pairs so well with a bite of orange at the same time- sweet and spicy. I left out the vegetable oil 2nd time and cooked scallops in olive oil and a pat of butter which gave them a delicious flavor. 2nd time made vinagarette ahead of time and placed it in the fridge for a few hours and it made it a little thicker which I liked better. Made a side of jasmine rice, baked parmesan asparagus with a arugula tangerine avocado jalapeño salad. Made it for 6 people and all raved about it!

This is my most-requested dinner by family and RV friends! Super easy and quick. I make a twist to this by adding a little mango to the blender, and then substitute mango slices for the orange slices,and garnish with cilantro. Also, a cast iron skillet and patted dry scallops are a must.

This was delicious! Only changes I made were to sub diced chili pepper (jalapeno too hot for me), and use honey mustard (to cut the tart vinegar a bit). Also added 1/4 tsp of spicy taco seasoning mix. Didn't have an orange, but did have a grapefruit, so added a little zest from it, then supremed the sections and added as a garnish, splashing a tiny bit of the juice into the dressing. Wonderful!

Used a can of mandarin oranges. Vinegarette was too tarte so added 2 slices of the orange and some juice from can till got flavor I liked. I seared scallops with my shrimp and added garlic powder to them in addition the cayenne and salt. Instead of pasta a lot of people paired with dish I served with Parmesan garlic mashed potatoes (no veggie with For first time in my life) and it was divine. Quick and simple- kept vinegarette in my ninja and pulsed it For last time just after plating the seafood so it was frothy. Can not wait to make again! Right blend of spicy and sweet. Thanks Chef John for the inspiration to a great meal!

This was so good. I adjusted the vinaigrette a bit. I used 2 large jalapenos, 2 cloves of garlic, and went half white wine vinegar, and half lime juice. Didn't bother with the orange segments. Will be making this again, many times, hubby loved it!
This was very tasty and I would make it again. I did not have any oranges so I used peaches and grilled them- it complemented the vinaigrette very well.

Excellent recipe! I did not use orange segments but that was just fine. I used left over vinaigrette for a pasta salad the next day. It was incredibly delicious. Marinated tomatoes overnight in vinaigrette and then added lots of veggies to cellentani pasta. OMG!! THANK YOU JOHN!!

I think is a 5 star recipe if you have the right scallops and a great pan. I used cast iron. Me being in the Midwest - the “right” bay scallops can be hard to come by but I really wanted to try this. I made sure they were really “dried” before starting this but even still - has to use a paper towel to soak up some of the juices halfway during the cooking process so they would sear as intended. Most turned out, some did not. The combination of flavors is amazing - even with mediocre scallops. Sweet, savory, a hint of spice! Served over couscous and a bed of spinach. Really enjoyed and would like to try again. Thanks again Chef John!

OMG this is a GREAT and simple recipe, thank you Chef John! My rendition I seared 8 XL scallops over a Himalayan salt block at extreme high heat. I added sautéed tomatoes at the end of the sear to infuse. I backed off the Dijon by 1 heaping tablespoon. (overpowers the vinaigrette for my taste)
I doubled the recipe. And, used three jalapeños and it was perfect! This was delicious. We even used the vinaigrette as dressing on our salad. And, made garlic mashed potatoes. Yum

I screwed up. I used wet pack scallops instead of Dry Pack Scallops. My scallops didn't sear because they released a ton of water. The fault was mine not Chef Johns. Make sure you follow his instructions mentioned in the video. - Dry Pack Scallops only

Have made this numerous times, exactly as written. It is the best scallop recipe we have ever had. I'm a Mainer so fresh, dry scallops are readily available here. Excellent as an appetizer or an entree.

I loved this. Hubs said the sauce didn’t do it for him. Did not serve with oranges. Served over couscous as another person recommended. It was perfect. Would be fancy enough for company if they like some heat. My garden jalapeños were pretty potent - my mouth is tingling pleasantly, but not everyone likes that :)
Made exactly as written. The vinaigrette is something else. We're already planning on how to use it in the other meals. So simple and it's so good.
I liked the dusting for the scallops before they are cooked in oil. I didn't like the sauce though.
Easy and totally wonderful

I only had 1 orange, but otherwise made exactly per the instructions. I did not reduce the amount of jalapeño, but it must have been a weak jalapeño because the dressing wasn’t at all spicy. It was ok, but I wouldn’t make it again.
I LOVE this dish. So bright, fresh and flavorful. I serve it with pearl cous cous and a green vegetable. Tonight, asparagus. Better than any restaurant meal.

I made this just as directed. I made the vinaigrette early in the afternoon so it had time to rest and develop. I used a very large jalapeño. I cut up the orange sections as directed- no pith or membrane. Wow! What a fantastic combo. The mellow scallops with the fresh jalapeño vinaigrette and the sweet orange. Wonderful! Easy. Will def in make again. Thank you !!!
